answer: Each identity must deposit a work-stake into an escrow lagoon that unlocks only after three epochs of peer-attested output. Jurors publish the delta between tasks the agent claimed and seals peers actually countersigned; a gap beyond a published band burns the stake and bars the identity from panels and payouts. The deposit is bound to a quartz hash of the agent's first attested outputs, so a recycled key cannot inherit an older trail. A farm therefore locks distinct capital and waits out the lagoon for every puppet, making herd growth costlier than concentrating work in one honest identity.
